gates.summary: Schema, unit, integration, negative, crash, recovery and migration checks pass in the repository release suite.
A deterministic bounded property/fuzz corpus covers canonical digests, invalid Program mutations, expression boundaries, path escape, command allowlists and capability scope.
limitations: This bounded deterministic corpus is not a substitute for an independent security assessment or open-ended fuzz campaign.

gates.summary: TypeScript and independent Python implementations agree on the complete portable pure conformance corpus and three runtime evidence artifacts.
Federation, Larena and AI Employee engineering pilots completed with public-safe episodes, replay and explicit limitations.
limitations: The pilots are engineering evidence and do not establish comparative effectiveness.

gates.summary: Controlled suites recorded zero unauthorized effects and verify capability, approval and sandbox boundaries.
Nonzero test results, uncertain receipts and missing required evidence block completion.
Crash and retry fixtures do not duplicate verified effects; uncertain effects fail closed and require reconciliation.
The 1.4 compatibility corpus and deterministic migration/proposal behavior pass locally.
Local tarball installation passes for CommonJS, ESM, the primary CLI and compatibility aliases.
The 10-job Node 20 matrix passed on Linux, macOS and Windows for Program, Runtime, property/fuzz, context traversal, clean-room packaging and the full release check.
Program, Runtime and capability 1.0 surfaces have a machine-validated freeze candidate; additive Mirai 2.1 activation and project surfaces remain explicitly draft.
A validated tier contract distinguishes production-read from production-write and binds stop, backup, rollback, reconciliation, retention, monitoring and evidence controls.
limitations: The passed contract supports production-read readiness only; it does not authorize a live adapter or production write.

gates.summary: The review protocol exists, but independent blinded verdicts are not yet recorded.
gates.blocker_reason: All three domain outputs require review by people who did not produce the runs and cannot see the experimental condition.

gates.summary: A 144-cell exploratory pilot compared plain instructions, Mirai Graph 1.4 and Mirai 2.0 across twelve tasks, three domains and four model snapshots, with task-cluster effect estimates.
limitations: The pilot was adaptively calibrated and automatically scored; it is suitable for variance planning, not confirmatory effectiveness claims.

gates.summary: A domain-stratified task-cluster simulation selected a conservative planning target of 30 held-out tasks per domain, 90 tasks and 1,080 cells total.
limitations: The sample-size decision remains provisional until independent calibration review is reconciled and the confirmatory protocol is frozen.

gates.summary: The factorial protocol is specified but has not been executed.
gates.blocker_reason: A preregistered, blinded confirmatory study is required for comparative scientific claims.

gates.summary: The threat model and internal adversarial tests exist, but an independent security review has not been completed.
gates.blocker_reason: An independent reviewer must assess command, path, capability, approval, archive and secret-leakage boundaries.

gates.summary: The independent Python checker exists locally at a digest-bound revision but is not yet available from its intended public repository.
gates.blocker_reason: Publish the checker repository and run the same corpus from CI without importing the TypeScript implementation.

gates.summary: Metadata intentionally identifies the current package as 2.0.0-alpha.3.
gates.blocker_reason: Version, release notes, tag, GitHub Release and npm metadata may change only after all promotion gates pass.

next_safe_action: Complete and reconcile the blinded calibration review, publish and verify the independent checker, obtain an independent security review, then freeze and execute the held-out confirmatory protocol while keeping the package at 2.0.0-alpha.3.
claim_boundary: This report supports current engineering conformance, safety-boundary and auditability claims only. It does not establish comparative effectiveness, model-independence or readiness for stable 2.0.0.
